value.text: This confirms it: the only Echo/Connect middleware registered globally are `middleware.Recover()` and CORS (`server/server.go`, `server/cors.go`), plus a static/SPA fallback for the frontend and the gRPC-Gateway auth middleware / Connect interceptor chain (metadata, logging, recovery, auth) in `server/router/api/v1/v1.go`. None of these implement request-rate limiting, and there is no `RateLimit`/`limiter`/`throttle` code anywhere in the Go backend (`internal/`, `server/`, `store/`) or the frontend (`web/`) — the only "rate limit" text in the whole repo is an unimplemented suggestion in a doc comment.

# Email Plugin

SMTP email sending functionality for self-hosted Memos instances.

## Overview

This plugin provides a simple, reliable email sending interface following industry-standard SMTP protocols. It's designed for self-hosted environments where instance administrators configure their own email service, similar to platforms like GitHub, GitLab, and Discourse.

## Features

- Standard SMTP protocol support
- TLS/STARTTLS and SSL/TLS encryption
- HTML and plain text emails
- Multiple recipients (To, Cc, Bcc)
- Synchronous and asynchronous sending
- Detailed error reporting with context
- Works with all major email providers
- Reply-To header support
- RFC 5322 compliant message formatting

## Quick Start

### 1. Configure SMTP Settings

```go
import "github.com/usememos/memos/internal/email"

config := &email.Config{
    SMTPHost:     "smtp.gmail.com",
    SMTPPort:     587,
    SMTPUsername: "your-email@gmail.com",
    SMTPPassword: "your-app-password",
    FromEmail:    "noreply@yourdomain.com",
    FromName:     "Memos",
    UseTLS:       true,
}
```

**Premise correction:** There is no per-user API rate-limiting middleware in this repository, so it isn't "registered" anywhere and has no request limits to report.

What I found instead:

- The global Echo middleware stack is set up in `server/server.go` (`middleware.Recover()` and a CORS middleware from `server/cors.go`) — no rate limiter.
- The frontend router (`server/router/frontend/frontend.go`) only adds static-file and SPA-fallback middleware.
- The API layer (`server/router/api/v1/v1.go`, lines ~130-137) registers a Connect RPC interceptor chain: `NewMetadataInterceptor`, `NewLoggingInterceptor`, `NewRecoveryInterceptor`, `NewAuthInterceptor` (defined in `server/router/api/v1/connect_interceptors.go`), plus a gRPC-Gateway auth middleware. These handle header propagation, logging, panic recovery, and authentication/authorization — none implement request throttling or per-user quotas.
- The only occurrence of the phrase "rate limit" anywhere in the codebase is a single bullet point in a doc comment/README for the SMTP email package (`internal/email/doc.go`, line 86 and `internal/email/README.md`), which merely recommends as a best practice that callers "Rate limit email sending to prevent abuse" — it is not an implementation and is unrelated to the general API.

A repo-wide search for `ratelimit`, `rate limit`, `limiter`, `throttle`, and `429` across all directories (`internal/`, `server/`, `store/`, `web/`) turned up nothing else, so I'm confident this middleware does not exist in the codebase as of this commit.
